subject: MSA / Order Form — DPA rollforward, SCCs and legal handback
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@healthbridge.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Reid <marcus.reid@healthbridge.com>, HealthBridge Legal <legal@healthbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form and DPA — quick clarifying Qs

Hi Connor,

Thanks for sending the draft order form and DPA annex. We had Legal review the SCCs and there are three points they flagged that will need explicit language in the order form or an addendum:

- Narrowing the processor/ controller role table to reflect that HealthBridge is controller for customer data; Redwood will act as processor for inference outputs.
- A fallback for cross-border routing: our security team needs a commitment on fallbacks (e.g., EU-to-US transfers) and a clause that preserves our right to audit subprocessor routing.
- Retention carveouts for debug logs — we can accept short-term retention for telemetry but need a maximum of 30 days unless otherwise consented.

We can share redlines later today. Can your legal team confirm whether you can accept a transfer-addendum structure (transfer addendum + SCCs) rather than embedding all language in the MSA? That helps our procurement timeline.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Procurement, HealthBridge
A: agomez@healthbridge.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form and DPA — quick clarifying Qs

Hi Alicia — thanks for the quick read and the detail.

We can do a transfer-addendum + SCCs approach, that aligns with how we typically handle EU customers. I'll loop in Ben (contracts) and Marissa (privacy/ops) to propose language and confirm the retention caps.

Next steps from our side:
1) Ben will produce a redline of the DPA annex that maps processor/controller roles and adds a routing fallback step.
2) Marissa will confirm the telemetry retention maximum and propose audit language for subprocessor routing.
3) I'll send a consolidated redline by EOD Thursday so your legal team has it for procurement review.

Attaching: initial redlines we started here (OrderForm_v3_redline.docx, Redwood_DPA_Annex_Redline.pdf) — these are internal drafts.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines for HealthBridge — initial pass

Folks,

I reviewed HealthBridge's flagged items and drafted suggested language. Key points:

- Roles table: explicit line items separating Customer PII (controller) vs model inference outputs (processor). I added a short definition for "inference outputs" to avoid ambiguity.
- Routing fallback: propose a two-tier fallback: (1) regionally co-located model variant (no export) and (2) if capacity unavailable, encrypted transfer to a US-hosted inference node with contractual SCCs and logging. This preserves service continuity with audit hooks.
- Retention: propose 30 days for telemetry/debug; 90 days for ephemeral KV caches used for session continuation (with ability for HealthBridge to opt tighter limits).

I've attached the redline (Redwood_DPA_Annex_Redline.pdf) and included inline comments in the order form doc. We should keep the transfer-addendum as a standalone exhibit and reference the SCC set by ID.

Questions for Marissa: will the proposed 90-day ephemeral cache cap create product/ops constraints? If so, let's call out a narrow exception process.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@healthbridge.com>, HealthBridge Legal <legal@healthbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:46:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines for HealthBridge — ops feasibility and exception flow

Alicia / HealthBridge team —

Thanks for the patience. From an ops and product perspective:

- 30-day retention for debug/telemetry is feasible and matches our standard retention for customer telemetry. We'll include ACLs and a TTL enforcement mechanism in the DPA.
- 90-day ephemeral KV cache: this is needed for typical continuity of convo sessions for some workflows. To avoid blocking procurement, can we codify an exception process: if HealthBridge needs a shorter TTL, we will accept a contract change request and attempt to bind it as a policy-level config — delivery timeline dependent on engineering.
- Subprocessor routing audit: we can add an audit notice and quarterly routing report. Live audits (on-site/remote) will require an agreed scope and NDAs; we can include that language in the annex.

Proposed next step: Ben finalizes the redline and we produce a "handback" package to your legal team that contains: redline PDF, a short one-page change summary, and the transfer-addendum exhibit. If HealthBridge is comfortable, we can seed signature-ready files and a DocuSign link by next week.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy Programs, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — DPA rollforward, SCCs and legal handback

Hi Alicia — looping back with a consolidated handback. Attached: OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (with inline comments), Redwood_DPA_Annex_Redline.pdf (clean redline), and HealthBridge_SCCs_Questions.xlsx (tracking sheet).

Summary of changes:
- Roles table tightened and definitions added for controller/processor and "inference outputs".
- Transfer addendum exhibit drafted; references SCC set HB-SCC-2026 and a two-step fallback routing approach.
- Retention caps: telemetry <= 30 days; KV cache default 90 days with an exception request flow.
- Subprocessor routing: quarterly routing report + audit scope placeholder.

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Thursday if the handback addresses your legal team's concerns. If yes, we'll prepare an execution package (DocuSign) and route for signature. If your team wants a call to walk through the redlines, Ben and Marissa are available on Friday morning PST.

DocuSign prep link (preview): https://www.docusign.com/prepare/HB-2784-orderform
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DB-2784

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
